item.title: Trump's Smart Iran Exit
item.description: Jon Alterman argues in the Times of India that Trump was right to end the Iran war, not because the U.S. won, but because the conflict exposed the limits of military power, reshaped U.S.-Israel ties, and showed the value of diplomacy and partners like India.

item.title: Venezuela Suffered Its Worst Earthquake in Decades: What Comes Next?
item.description: Two powerful earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 on the Richter scale, recently struck along the coast of Venezuela. The international response will be a major test of U.S. leadership and Washington's new relationship with Caracas.

item.title: AI Has a Memory Problem
item.description: As AI data centers consume a growing share of global memory supply, shortages of advanced memory chips are emerging as a critical constraint on AI deployment and industrial competitiveness. Policymakers must expand memory and packaging capacity to avoid future bottlenecks.

item.title: The Greenspan Lesson for the AI Race
item.description: Senior Fellow Karl Smith argues that Chair Greenspan’s legacy offers a lesson for the AI era: macroeconomic data is backward-looking. If U.S. institutions misread a new productivity shift, they risk higher rates, slower AI investment, and a weaker long-term tech position.

item.title: Anthropic and the Export Control Dilemma
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch discusses the use of export controls on Anthropic's latest models and examines the tradeoff between measures that may hinder industry competitiveness and the risk that, without such controls, advanced technologies could fall into the hands of adversaries.

item.title: Lebanon in the Shadow of the U.S.-Iran MOU: Risks and Opportunities
item.description: The diplomacy underway to end the U.S.-Israel-Iran war could deepen Lebanon's strategic setbacks—or it could provide a historic opportunity to advance key Lebanese interests and contribute to a more stable regional order.

item.title: States Weekly: June 24, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers June 24, 2026.

item.title: After Maduro: Human Trafficking and the Vulnerability of Venezuelan Migrants in Colombia
item.description: The fragile security situations in both Colombia and Venezuela create conditions that allow criminal and non-state armed groups to expand trafficking in persons.
